_readme: A fight with two people in it, played. Everything BattleLogic proves about a round is
proved there; what only a played fight can show is that the round reaches the player -
that the menu is asked twice, that the second asking is a different person's, and that
both of them come out of it with their own numbers changed.
The command menu is Attack, Magic, Item, Flee. With two members the FIRST press is the
leader's order and the menu comes straight back for Rook's, which is the whole shape of
command-all-then-resolve: two confirms before anything happens at all.
Counts are deliberate here, and they are counts of ROWS rather than of tiles: the walk
legs are still held against geometry. Rook is at village [1,8] against the west wall,
which is the one approach a body cannot be slid past.
The xp is the assertion that says the DQ rule is running: one slink pays 5, and both of
them get all of it. FF1 would divide it and this would read 2 and 2.

steps.text: fetch Rook: south to the well, west to the wall, south to her

north up the wall and through the west door. The hold CARRIES past the warp - an arriving leg keeps walking in the next map - so the next leg re-anchors against the hollow's own geometry rather than assuming where this one stopped.
south down the east side until the wall, then west along the only row that reaches the gap the slink is standing in
TWO orders before anything happens. Attack for the leader, then the menu comes back for Rook - that is command-all-then-resolve, and one confirm would not be enough to start the round.
the round plays out; mash the rest of the fight through
both of them earn the FULL award, which is Dragon Quest's rule - FF1 divides it and this would read 2 and 3

and the enemy swung at ROOK, not at the player: she is down three and he is untouched. That is the target draw reaching the party at all - with the enemy always aiming at whoever is first, this reads 17 and 24.
